claims.text: The initial alloy is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The initial CoCrFeNiTi alloy has a simple crystal structure.
Adding carbon to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi will improve hardness and mechanical performance.
Adding carbon will preserve the favorable plasticity of CoCrFeNiTi.
Adding carbon will preserve the favorable machinability of CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed material can be processed by ball milling followed by SPS at 2200 °C, a 100 °C/min heating rate, 30 MPa uniaxial pressure, and a 5-minute dwell under vacuum or argon.
Carbon addition and the specified processing will form a homogeneous high-entropy metal-carbide phase.
The resulting carbide will have a single-phase rock-salt FCC structure.
The entropy-forming-ability descriptor predicts the synthesizability of disordered five-metal refractory carbides as homogeneous high-entropy single phases.
Formation of the predicted homogeneous carbide phase will improve hardness and mechanical performance.
The carbon-modified alloy will have at least 20% greater Vickers hardness than unmodified equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed intervention applies to processing at temperatures no greater than 2200 °C and pressures no greater than 30 MPa.
Carbon addition is expected to produce a significant increase in elastic modulus relative to the unmodified alloy.
The exact carbon content and optimal processing conditions are unknown.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 20% hardness increase, but the falsification rule uses an undefined 'significant' increase and only falsifies when hardness, modulus, and phase formation all fail together. Thus, a hardness increase below 20% could violate the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
